X.note: The wall and street rendering is strong, but the soldiers are a smeared, translucent, ghosted mass of figurines. Limbs are mangled and faces are missing. The figures don't sit in the scene: they're semi-transparent and have no grounded shadows.

Y.note: Same strong environment. The figures are more legible and have clear coats, facings, cross-belts and tricorns, but they look like painted wooden or plastic toy soldiers. They have stiff poses, smooth shapes, near-identical faces and ill-fitting scale and lighting against the textured walls.

why: Y's soldiers read as distinct, coherent British redcoats in a plausible formation, whereas X's figures are a ghosted, blurry blob that looks broken.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the translucent figure cluster with fewer, solid, properly scaled soldiers (6-10) with real cloth texture, cast contact shadows on the dirt and consistent lighting. Add some civilians and rubble, and keep the pose variety natural.
anachronisms_seen: Blue-coated figures in X that look like French or Spanish troops or a mixed-up uniform scheme, in a British-held town
Modern-looking glossy shutters and window glazing
Flag looks too crisp and modern in scale and fold, flying on a pole with no visible structure
Near-pristine uniforms with no siege wear
